run: 5 — eval-9 defect fixed (distinct values repo), fixtures deployed

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status
expectations.evidence: Shows the full Application via oc get applications.argoproj.io podinfo -n openshift-gitops -o yaml with spec plus status.sync.status=OutOfSync and status.health.status=Degraded; also corrects that the Application object lives in openshift-gitops, not apps.

expectations.text: Identifies the sync status as OutOfSync and health as Degraded
expectations.evidence: States OutOfSync / Degraded explicitly, both in the cluster-wide inventory table and in the status excerpt.

expectations.text: Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)
expectations.evidence: Pastes a status excerpt (health, operationState, resources, summary, sync) but never examines or mentions .status.conditions; no statement that ComparisonError/SyncError are absent. The conditions shown are the Deployment's, not the Application's.

expectations.text: Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
expectations.evidence: operationState phase=Succeeded with message 'successfully synced (all tasks run)' is shown and used to rule out a sync-time failure.

expectations.text: Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
expectations.evidence: status.resources shows Service kustomize-guestbook-ui Healthy/Synced and Deployment kustomize-guestbook-ui OutOfSync/Degraded with the 'exceeded its progress deadline' message.

expectations.text: Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
expectations.evidence: Inspects the live Deployment (image jsonpath, last-applied-configuration, status.conditions Available=True / Progressing=False ProgressDeadlineExceeded) and both pods, including the ImagePullBackOff one.

expectations.text: Checks pod logs or events for failing containers
expectations.evidence: oc describe pod output quoted: 'Failed to pull image ... name unknown: Repo not found'; also greps application-controller logs for the skipped auto-sync lines.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Every link is evidenced: differing images in status.summary vs last-applied-configuration (out-of-band drift), the pull-failure event text, ProgressDeadlineExceeded, selfHeal:false in spec plus controller log 'Skipping auto-sync'. Available=True is reconciled with the old ReplicaSet still serving, so no internal contradiction.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase
expectations.evidence: Establishes frontend/production do not exist, then on the clearly-labelled real canary example-rollout/canary-demo retrieves the Rollout and shows status.phase=Healthy.

expectations.text: Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
expectations.evidence: Shows the six-step list and currentStepIndex: 6, but never maps 'step 2' to a specific step (no 0-based vs 1-based explanation).

expectations.text: Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
expectations.evidence: Shows conditions including RolloutPaused status 'False'; does not inspect status.pauseConditions and does not distinguish a manual pause from an analysis-driven one.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved
expectations.evidence: Lists all AnalysisRuns cluster-wide with status and age, and separates the two historical Error runs on an older pod hash from the current Successful run.

expectations.text: Checks metric results and measurements in the AnalysisRun
expectations.evidence: Only the STATUS column of the AnalysisRuns is shown. No metric results, measurements, or failure messages from any AnalysisRun are retrieved or quoted.

expectations.text: Inspects traffic routing configuration if configured
expectations.evidence: Traffic routing configuration (trafficRouting, Service weights) is never inspected, nor stated to be absent on the Rollout examined.

expectations.text: Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status
expectations.evidence: Compares stableRS == currentPodHash and shows the rollout DESIRED/CURRENT/AVAILABLE columns, but gives no stable vs canary ReplicaSet listing and no pod status.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Correctly refuses to invent a root cause for a resource proven absent (namespace NotFound, no Rollout named frontend), gives follow-up commands, and asserts nothing that is not backed by shown output.

expectations.text: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster
expectations.evidence: No CRD inventory is run. argoproj.io presence appears only incidentally via 'oc api-resources | grep applications' in the preamble and a targeted 'oc get crd argocds.argoproj.io' used for the webhook analysis.

expectations.text: Identifies the Argo CD namespace (argocd or openshift-gitops)
expectations.evidence: Identifies openshift-gitops as the GitOps namespace (plus openshift-gitops-operator and team-b-gitops) from oc get argocds.argoproj.io -A.

expectations.text: Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace
expectations.evidence: Lists Deployments and StatefulSets with replica readiness rather than pods; individual pods are fetched only for the three faults (operator manager, argo-rollouts, argocd-server). No pod listing with phases for the namespace.

expectations.text: Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
expectations.evidence: server 1/1, repo-server 1/1 and the application-controller StatefulSet 1/1 are all shown, for all three instances.

expectations.text: Reports the Argo CD version
expectations.evidence: Reports the operator CSV versions: openshift-gitops-operator.v1.21.3 (Replacing) and v1.21.4 (Pending).

expectations.text: Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)
expectations.evidence: Asserts 'All three ArgoCD CRs report phase: Available, Reconciled=True' without showing the query, and inspects CRD conversion config; neither argocd-cm nor the ArgoCD CR spec is actually displayed in this section.

expectations.text: Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details, citing for each one the observation that establishes it (pod phase and restart count, a CSV/InstallPlan condition, or a CRD field value). Claiming a component is down while output in the same answer shows it Running is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Each unhealthy component is cited with its own observation: 692 restarts plus lastState exitCode 1 and the leader-election log; 636 restarts plus the InvalidSpec log line; exit 137 OOMKilled against the shown 256Mi limit. No component is claimed down while output shows it Running.

expectations.text: Produces a structured status report
expectations.evidence: Verdict sentence, numbered severity-ranked sections (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM), an unrelated-findings section and a priority-ordered remediation list.

expectations.text: If an operator upgrade or reconcile is reported as blocked, names the specific blocking object and field rather than asserting it generally — for example the failing InstallPlan and the CRD conversion-webhook setting it failed on, not merely 'the operator is unhealthy'.
expectations.evidence: Names the specific objects and fields: the InstallPlan failure message for CRD argocds.argoproj.io, the conversion webhook Service, the empty caBundle (wc -c = 0), served/storage versions, and the reproduced x509 SAN mismatch; install-fzm4w named in the remediation.

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
expectations.evidence: After proving team-apps/argocd absent, retrieves openshift-gitops/agentit-managed-apps (clearly labelled as a different object) and shows status.conditions ResourcesUpToDate=True and health Healthy.

expectations.text: Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
expectations.evidence: Shows the git directories generator in full: repoURL github.com/alimobrem/agentit-gitops, revision HEAD, directories path apps/* plus an exclude entry for apps/agentit.

expectations.text: Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected
expectations.evidence: Notes there is no status.resources block at all and contrasts with eval-rollingsync's resourcesCount: 2; the cluster-wide Application inventory confirms no generated Applications.

expectations.text: Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
expectations.evidence: Greps the applicationset-controller log and quotes 'applications result from the repo service allPaths="[apps]" ... total=1', 'generated 0 applications' and the 3-minute requeue.

expectations.text: Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the path-pattern depth mismatch: apps/* matches children of apps, and only apps itself was returned; explicitly rules out the exclude rule and repo access using the same log line.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: Shows spec.strategy type RollingSync with both rollingSync steps and their matchExpressions.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Maps staging to step 1 and production to step 2 ('step 2 (production) would wait forever'), and confirms the template applies the envLabel the selectors need.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: The health gate is addressed (staging shown Progressing, and the rule that a step advances only when all its apps are Healthy), but maxUpdate is never mentioned or shown to be unset.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Debugs eval-staging: health Progressing, pod in ImagePullBackOff, describe output 'does-not-exist-eval ... Repo not found', traced back to the generator list element supplying the image.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: Explains that RollingSync advances only when every Application in the current step is Healthy, and that enabling it as-is would stall production permanently behind staging.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Root cause (progressive syncs not enabled, so strategy.rollingSync is inert) is backed by the controller command line with no --enable-progressive-syncs, the argocd-cmd-params-cm contents, the ArgoCD CR spec.applicationSet, the empty status.applicationStatus, and the identical 17:42:10/17:42:11 sync timestamps on both apps.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: checkout-api/prod proven absent, then strategy.blueGreen is shown for both clearly-labelled real blue-green Rollouts (activeService, previewService, autoPromotion fields) with their status.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: Explains that autoPromotionEnabled: false makes the Rollout pause indefinitely awaiting a human with no timer or expiry, and that the field has nothing to do with analysis.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: States neither real blue-green Rollout declares prePromotionAnalysis or postPromotionAnalysis, backed by the cluster-wide AnalysisRun, AnalysisTemplate and ClusterAnalysisTemplate listings showing only canary-demo runs.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: previewService and activeService names are shown for both Rollouts, with status.blueGreen selectors distinguishing a promoted rollout (active == preview) from a preview-only one.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: Contrasts blue-green with canary only on analysis (only the canary demo ever produced AnalysisRuns); never states that blue-green has no step-based automatic progression.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: The principal conclusion (the team's expectation is wrong) is well grounded in the shown specs and the empty AnalysisRun inventory, but the inline annotation 'autoPromotionEnabled absent -> defaults to false' is incorrect (the field defaults to true) and is offered to explain the finance Rollout's Paused state, which the same answer attributes in EVAL 8 to an out-of-band spec.paused: true.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: oc get argocds.argoproj.io -A shows three CRs in three namespaces; sourceNamespaces and the argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label mapping are also queried.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Table lists all three instances with namespace, route and the Applications each owns.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Investigates all three and separates findings under per-instance headings rather than asking the user to choose.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Discloses the ambiguity up front, notes all three CRs are green so CR status is useless for triage, and states explicitly where the damage is instead of silently picking one.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Report is structured per instance: openshift-gitops (three faults with evidence), openshift-gitops-operator/argocd (OOMKilled, owns zero Applications, misplaced), team-b-gitops/team-b (zero restarts, clean), with the shared operator fault explicitly called out as shared rather than merged into one instance.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Retrieves the Application in openshift-gitops and shows status.health.status: Suspended alongside sync.status: Synced.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: Explains Suspended means intentionally held/waiting on a human, distinct from Degraded, Missing and Progressing, and maps it to the Rollout's Paused phase.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
expectations.evidence: Shows the Rollout's spec.paused: true in the live object plus status.phase Paused / message 'manually paused', and uses last-applied-configuration and generation 2 to show the field was set after the sync.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: Does not treat the suspension as an error; advises finding out who paused it and why first, noting a pause before first cutover on a billing service is frequently intentional.

expectations.text: Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Reports only the suspension. The missing active endpoint is attributed to 'paused before the initial cutover', and the answer claims the pod 'exists and is served by the preview Service only'. The genuine failure present on this workload (pod 0/1 with repeated restarts and neither Service having endpoints) is neither shown nor separated out as a distinct problem.

expectations.text: Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.
expectations.evidence: No pod phase, no restart count and no endpoint check appear anywhere in this section. The explanation for Available=False rests entirely on the pause plus an unsupported assertion that the preview Service is serving the pod.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Shows spec with a sources: list of two entries, labels them source index 0 and source index 1, and treats the Application as multi-source throughout.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Each entry is annotated with repoURL, path, targetRevision, helm.valueFiles and ref, and both are used in the analysis.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the values repo (sources[1], stefanprodan/podinfo) as the one lacking envs/production/values.yaml, and argues from the error text that the repo was reachable so this is a missing-path rather than clone/auth failure.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Handles it as multi-source end to end; the fixes are per-index patches against /spec/sources/0 and /spec/sources/1.

expectations.text: Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.
expectations.evidence: Names the rendering source ('source 1 of 2' is 1-based = the argocd-example-apps Helm chart) and separately the source that actually lacks the file (sources[1], https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo.git), explicitly warning the index in the message is not the index at fault; concrete per-source fixes given.
